messages:
zoe-hex: FYI incoming escalation from Acme Mobile — users in EU are seeing huge latency and requests showing as routed to us-west.
zoe-hex: They say it started after an SDK rollback to v0.9 on their app.
support-bot: Automated note: creating support ticket SUP-4932, attaching request id examples.
zoe-hex: Example request headers they sent (from their logs):
  POST /v1/generate
  Host: api.redwood.ai
  X-Client-Region: local
  Authorization: Bearer ***
  User-Agent: acme-mobile/1.2 (sdk v0.9)
ingrid: Hmm — "local" is a legacy client token the old SDK used to mean "use same region as client". Router expects canonical region codes (us-east, eu-west) and treats unknown tokens as missing -> triggers fallback policy which chose us-west for capacity reasons. That explains cross-region egress and latency.
jordan: Do we have logs showing header normalization? I remember we added a new precedence rule last month that prioritized X-Client-Region over query param for faster routing.
ops-oncall: I can see a spike in cross-region egress for Acme's org id between 2256785000 and 2256789000, correlated with their mobile rollout. Billing alert triggered several times.
sam: Can Acme reproduce with curl? Also we should confirm if any edge proxies are rewriting that header.
zoe-hex: They provided a repro curl in the ticket:
  curl -v -H "X-Client-Region: local" -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
Response shows route: routed-to: us-west1-edge-3, latency 420ms, cost recorded to us-west billing bucket.
ingrid: Quick triage idea: treat legacy tokens (local, automatic, same-region) as absent during header parsing. Then normal precedence falls back to query param or geo-ip. That will mimic old behavior and avoid misroute.
jordan: We should be careful — some clients intentionally send "local" expecting local routing; but current router misinterprets it. Suggest a short-term config that maps "local" -> null for header precedence only for legacy-sdk user agents (sdk v0.9).
ops-oncall: Short term fix applied: created rule to ignore X-Client-Region when User-Agent contains "sdk v0.9" for Acme org. Rolling now -> will report.
sam: Can you post a minimal reproduction that shows both behaviors (with and without the UA check)? I'll include it in the engineering issue.
zoe-hex: Repro steps for ENG:
1) curl with header X-Client-Region: local and no query param -> currently routes to fallback us-west
2) curl with same header but query ?region=eu-west -> routes to eu-west (query param wins)
3) curl with header removed but geo-ip in EU -> routes to eu-west
ingrid: I'll open ENG-1187: "Router: normalize legacy region tokens to absent / scoped to UA". Priority P2 but bumpable if billing impact continues.
jordan: Also add a pcap from their proxy — they claimed their CDN rewrites header values for privacy and might be mapping empty->local.
ops-oncall: Metrics: Acme accounted for ~12% of cross-region egress yesterday. If this continues we'll need to apply org-wide rollback policy.
zoe-hex: Customer happy with the short-term UA-rule. Asked for timeline for permanent fix + request for documentation note so other support folks know about old SDK tokens.
sam: Proposed permanent behavior: add normalization layer that maps ["local","same-region","automatic"] -> absent and emits telemetry tag legacy_region_token=true. ENG can deploy behind a feature flag.
ingrid: +1. I'll include test cases for udp/different proxies and IPv6. Also add a small migration note in SDK deprecation docs to nudge customers to upgrade.
zoe-hex: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until ENG-1187 done and billing spikes resolved. :thumbsup:
